title: Robustness of Mixtures of Experts to Feature Noise
claim: Under increasing activation sparsity, latent modular block structure emerges in real model activations, motivating a modular-computation view.
layout: 3 heatmap panels, left-to-right, each with its own colorbar
description: Three square heatmaps sit side by side, each with Samples on the vertical axis and Features on the horizontal axis. Each has a viridis colorbar on its right. They show Llama-2-7B layer-0 up_proj input activation percentiles after 0%, 40% and 70% uniform sparsity pruning. The left panel is mostly noisy green and teal with a few dark horizontal bands, so little structure is visible. In the middle panel the background darkens and a diagonal staircase of small bright yellow-green blocks appears in the lower half. In the right panel the background is almost uniformly dark purple, and the diagonal blocks are crisp and bright, which shows clear modular structure. The eye goes to the bright diagonal blocks on the dark background in the right panel. The colorbar ranges differ: roughly 0.1 to 0.8, 0.4 to 1.0, and 0.7 to 0.95.
caption: Modular structure in input activations to the up proj layer within the MLP block of layer-0 of the Llama-2-7B model, revealed using TEAL (Liu et al., 2025), for uniform magnitude pruning. From left to right, panels show activation percentiles after pruning activations based on 0%, 40%, and 70% uniform activation sparsity thresholds, respectively. Since the activation distributions are skewed due to the presence of outlier activations, we plot activation percentiles.
abstract: Despite their practical success, it remains unclear why Mixture of Experts (MoE) models can outperform dense networks beyond sheer parameter scaling. We study an iso-parameter regime where inputs exhibit latent modular structure but are corrupted by feature noise, a proxy for noisy internal activations. We show that sparse expert activation acts as a noise filter: compared to a dense estimator, MoEs achieve lower generalization error under feature noise, improved robustness to perturbations, and faster convergence speed. Empirical results on synthetic data and real-world language tasks corroborate the theoretical insights, demonstrating consistent robustness and efficiency gains from sparse modular computation.
